exposure: timing of vacuum extraction (early: <2 hours vs. delayed: >2 hours in the second stage of labor)
outcome: maternal composite adverse outcome (chorioamnionitis, 3-4 degree lacerations, postpartum hemorrhage [PPH])
cohort: The study included 2521 term singleton pregnancies delivered by vacuum extraction at a single university-affiliated medical center.
finding: Vacuum extraction performed up to 3 hours into the second stage of labor appears as safe as early vacuum extraction regarding maternal and neonatal outcomes, but extra caution is needed for extended second stages exceeding 3 hours.
mod_finding: Vacuum extraction performed in the late second stage of labor (up to 3 hours) is comparable in safety to early vacuum extraction for maternal and neonatal outcomes, though significant risks for specific outcomes (PPH, 5 min Apgar <=7, umbilical pH <7.0) were observed when the second stage exceeded 3 hours before becoming insignificant after multiregression analysis.
